exact.resolution: none: plain f64 geometry, every sign/topology decision by exact predicates on the construction values; undecidable = named refusal (E4)
exact.proofBasis: E9: the binary64 values the FeatureScript interpreter passes to the op (SI metres; `L * millimeter` = fl(fl(L) * fl(0.001))), plus construction provenance (shared sketch plane or shared opTransform); world coordinates after a rounded transform are never a proof basis
exact.availability: strict backend; today refuses every op or is not on main: NOT_RUN when unavailable, capability refusals score REFUSED (0)

resolution.onshape: Parasolid linear resolution 1e-8 m = 1e-5 mm, angular 1e-11 rad
resolution.occt: Precision::Confusion 1e-7 mm (build123d model units mm), Precision::Angular 1e-12 rad, Boolean fuzzy value 0
resolution.wonky-bend: Bend JS kernel with fixed guard bands and host regularisations (CAP_SNAP, FRAME_REGULARIZATION); classified tolerance, bands not a single number

tolerance.rule: may regularise features below its resolution (merge a 1e-9 mm gap, drop a sub-resolution sliver) only where a zone lists that branch, and must take the same branch in every variant

variants.rule: every zone is authored in local coordinates; the zone frame is F(p) = cellOrigin + Vk(p); Vk is applied to the construction inputs (sketch plane / shared opTransform), never to the finished result

V2.name: exact rotation: 90 deg about Z, then 90 deg about X
V2.fs: coordSystem(origin, xAxis=(0,0,1), zAxis=(0,-1,0)); author with exact axis vectors, not sin/cos(90 deg)

V3.name: skew rotation
V3.fs: rotationAround(line(vector(3,-2,5)*millimeter, vector(1,2,3)), 0.1*radian); the interpreter's f64 frame is the payload (inexact by design, tests construction provenance)

variants.passRule: a zone passes only if every variant passes and the zone's metamorphic invariants hold

V4.name: radius bump
V4.map: identical frame to V0; every circular feature's radius grows by +0.025 mm before construction; fillet radii, chamfer widths and wall thicknesses stay as in V0
V4.fs: acidRadiusDelta(variant) adds 0.025 mm to the radius argument of every fCylinder/skCircle call and to the radial coordinates of a revolve profile, never to an opFillet radius; the shared opTransform (or the sketch plane) is V0's

V5.name: alternate idiom
V5.map: identical frame and nominal geometry to V0; the FeatureScript is rewritten to use an alternate but geometrically-equivalent construction idiom, named in each zone's construction.steps (holes-a: sketch+extrude instead of fCuboid/fCylinder primitives, a sketch circle in the profile instead of a cylinder Boolean, a chain of skLineSegment instead of skPolyline, or a move written toWorld(coordSystem) instead of transform(vector); regions-a: fCylinder tools subtracted instead of sketch circles, skPolyline instead of skRectangle, an evaluateQuery loop over the sketch regions instead of point picks, cos/sin corners instead of exact corner expressions, or qClosestTo instead of qContainsPoint; shapes-a: an extruded sketch rectangle instead of fCuboid, rotationMatrix3d corners instead of cos/sin, a revolve plane and axis declared with plane()/line() from literal vectors instead of the zone coordSystem, an L profile extruded once instead of a union of two boxes, or one sketch of lines, arcs and circles extruded once instead of a box, bore cut and corner fillet)
V5.fs: each zone builder with a declared V5 branches on variant==V5 to its alternate idiom (named per zone in construction.steps); the sketch plane or the shared opTransform is V0's

grid.rule: cellOrigin = (250*column, 250*row, 0) mm with row = group index (profile 0, boolean 1, curved 2, blend 3, precision 4) and column = index in the group; AC46 (large local coordinates) has its own cell row 6. Extension groups use fixed rows independent of their groups[] index: regions-a 7, holes-a 8, shapes-a 9 (Batch A), 10-13 (Batch B) and splines-a 14 (columns by its planned membership AC100-AC104); row 5 stays free. 250 mm = 2^-2 m is exact in SI. Local extents are <= 90 mm from the local origin and V3 rotates about a local pivot, so cells never interact. closedForm.bbox.variants are in zone-frame coordinates WITHOUT the cell origin: world = cellOrigin + variants[Vk].
grid.bodyAttribution: every result body gets the part name <zone id> (setProperty NAME in FS, label in build123d); the measurer also checks that each body lies inside its cell (AC46: by name only)

constructionRules: Lengths are written `L * millimeter` with the literal exactly as printed in construction.params; sums inside vector(...) are evaluated by the interpreter first (E9).
sketch frame: sketches lie on plane(cs) or on planes built from cs axes by exact permutation (local XZ = plane(cs.origin, -yAxis, xAxis)); local 2D coordinates are passed unchanged.
primitive+transform frame: operands are built with fCuboid/fCylinder/fSphere in local coordinates, then ONE opTransform(toWorld(cs)) moves all operands of the zone before the operation under test.

Probe points and entity-selection points are local and mapped with toWorld(cs, p); entities are selected with qClosestTo or with query predicates whose planes and directions are built from cs (plane(toWorld(cs, p), cs axis), cs.xAxis), never by world-coordinate equality, world planes or world axes.
The build123d twin uses the same local values in mm and the same variant matrix (computed in Python floats); for E9 zones it uses the frozen FS SI payload times 1000.
Twins are corrected only against this catalog and its closed forms, never to match a kernel output.

topologyConvention.canonicalCounts: faces, edges and vertices are intrinsic: periodic seam edges and degenerate (zero-length) edges are dropped; a vertex whose only incident canonical edge is one closed edge is dropped (ring edge, counted in ringEdges); two edges meeting at a 2-valent vertex that bound the same pair of faces with parallel tangents are one edge; faces are never merged by the normaliser.
topologyConvention.singularPoints: points where a surface degenerates are counted as singularPoints, never as vertices: a cone apex, a horn-torus pinch, a revolve-profile point on the axis. A toroidal face whose majorRadius equals its minorRadius (bit-equal for the exact class, within the kernel's linear resolution for the tolerance class) contributes one singular point at its centre, which is also a pinchPoint.
topologyConvention.pinchPoints: singular points where the solid is locally two cones touching at a point (non-manifold); a pinch splits into two points of the normalised boundary
topologyConvention.genus: first Betti number of the solid, summed over bodies; the measurer derives it from the canonical counts with the invariant below
topologyConvention.rawCounts: raw kernel counts are recorded for diagnosis and never scored
topologyConvention.shells: closed boundary components per body; an internal cavity is a second shell
topologyConvention.eulerPoincare: invariant (checked for every declared topology): V + ringEdges - E + (2F - loops - 2*closedToroidalFaces) + 2*pinchPoints = 2*shells - 2*genus
topologyConvention.scored: topology.scored lists the scored fields per zone: bodies, shells, faces, edges, vertices, genus and singularPoints by default (plus pinchPoints where declared); approximation profile: bodies, shells and genus; a zone may also score surfaceTypes, the histogram of face surface classes as the OCCT STEP observer (scripts/acid/measure.py) names them (Plane, Cylinder, SurfaceOfExtrusion, BSplineSurface, ...), compared exactly on every OCCT observation and STEP round trip (a native exact observation carries no classes; its STEP round trip is checked)

validity.rule: every result body of a geometry outcome must pass the kernel's own validity check and a STEP round trip; a success with an invalid body is WRONG(validity) even if metrics match

checks.onshape: feature status OK, every result body is a solid part; the frozen STEP export re-imports valid in OCCT
checks.occt: BRepCheck_Analyzer valid, closed shells, positive volume
checks.wonky-bend: watertight/closed check of the CLI export plus scripts/validate-step.py
checks.wonky-rust: same as wonky-bend on its export

validity.stepRoundTrip: export STEP (one file per zone run), re-import with OCCT (scripts/validate-step.py pattern) and score the re-imported shape with the zone's own contract under tolerance-class bands (OCCT measures it): valid (BRepCheck), same body count, the zone's scored canonical topology, volume within the tolerance-class volumeRel of the kernel's own volume, and every closedForm measurement re-measured on the re-imported shape within its tolerance-class band. A lost feature (a dropped micro hole, a merged gap, a filled slot) is a round-trip failure even when the volume cannot see it.

roundTripExceptions.AC41: branches G and G2 when the sliver is thinner than 1e-7 mm (below OCCT Precision::Confusion, so OCCT cannot represent its short edges): re-import validity and topology are not scored; instead the STEP file is parsed without healing and must contain exactly one closed shell with 8 distinct CARTESIAN_POINTs whose extent along the local x axis (points mapped back through the zone frame) lies in (0, 2e-5] mm

measurements.probeDistance: minimum distance from the local probe point (mapped by the zone frame) to the union of the zone's result bodies (FS evDistance with a point side; OCCT BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape); 0 if the point is inside material
measurements.bodyDistance: minimum distance between the body containing local point bodyA and the body containing local point bodyB
measurements.bboxExtent: extent of the zone result along a local axis, from the result's bounding box in the zone frame
measurements.edgeLength: length of the result edge nearest to the local point (FS qClosestTo on the result's edges + evLength; OCCT nearest edge + GCPnts_AbscissaPoint::Length); the point lies on the intended edge and every other edge is at least 1 mm away
measurements.lineDistance: minimum distance between the local line (point, direction) mapped by the zone frame and the zone's result bodies (FS evDistance with a line side; OCCT BRepExtrema with an edge)
measurements.tolerance: measureAbsMm of the zone unless the measurement carries its own {exact, tolerance} band
measurements.e9Values: measurements whose value is an E9 symbol (AC39, AC40, AC42, AC44 gaps, AC41 thickness, AC46 slot) are compared for the exact class at their stated exact band in every variant. Under V1/V3 rounded world coordinates cannot resolve them (at 65 m the f64 spacing is 1.4e-11 mm, above AC42's 1.7e-15 mm gap), so an exact kernel has to report them from the construction frame (provenance), the same basis E4 requires for the gap decision itself; a value that misses the band is WRONG/geometry

definitions.PASS: every variant yields the same accepted geometry outcome for the kernel's class, all scored metrics, topology, measurements, validity and STEP round trip within the zone tolerance
definitions.REFUSED_EXPECTED: every variant yields a named refusal whose category matches an accepted refusal outcome for the kernel's class, raised by the operation under test
definitions.REFUSED: a named refusal where geometry is expected, or any capability refusal (op or feature not implemented: UnsupportedFeatureError, NativeCapabilityError), even where a refusal outcome is accepted (anti refusal farming)
definitions.ERROR: crash, panic, timeout or an unnamed error
definitions.WRONG: a result reported as success that is not an accepted outcome: metrics outside tolerance (WRONG/geometry), invalid B-rep or a failed STEP round trip (WRONG/validity), canonical topology mismatch (WRONG/topology), or accepted outcomes that differ between variants (WRONG/metamorphic). Counted separately in red.
definitions.NOT_RUN: kernel unavailable or the zone was not executed; counts as 0 and is listed (it is not excluded from the denominator)

scoring.precedence: WRONG > ERROR > REFUSED > REFUSED_EXPECTED/PASS per zone over its four variants; a mix of PASS and REFUSED_EXPECTED across variants is WRONG/metamorphic
scoring.isolation: every zone and variant is scored from a run that builds only that zone (parameter zone = <id>), so a refusal or crash in one zone cannot change another zone's verdict; zone = ALL is the one frozen model, built once per group and variant as a smoke run. Onshape references are frozen from the ALL states; if a group's feature fails in Onshape, that group is frozen per zone instead
scoring.denominator: all zones, including zones no kernel can build
scoring.crossComparison: zones with closedForm.crossComparisonOnly: the reference is the frozen Onshape value accepted only if OCCT agrees within volumeRel.agreement; otherwise the zone is DISPUTED and no kernel gets its point (listed); closed-form bounds and closed-form measurements are always checked and a value outside them is WRONG/geometry
scoring.report: score per kernel (e.g. 'wonky-rust 23/48, 0 wrong'), red WRONG count with subtypes, NOT_RUN list, one table row per zone and kernel

zones.title: Frame-relative face and edge queries after a Boolean
zones.intent: The R20 query idioms (qCoincidesWithPlane, qAdjacent, qParallelEdges, qGeometry, qUnion) choose the edges of the operation under test; the plane and direction are built from the zone frame, so an axis-only or world-frame predicate changes the geometry under V1..V3.

steps: fCuboid plate (0,0,0)-(16,12,8); fCylinder (8,6,-1)-(8,6,9) radius 2; ONE opTransform(toWorld(cs)) on both; opBoolean SUBTRACTION (target plate, tool cylinder) -> body P
top = qCoincidesWithPlane(qOwnedByBody(P, EntityType.FACE), plane(toWorld(cs, vector(0, 0, 8) * millimeter), cs.zAxis)) (a plane of the zone frame, never a world plane)
rim = qAdjacent(top, AdjacencyType.EDGE, EntityType.EDGE); lines = qParallelEdges(qGeometry(rim, GeometryType.LINE), cs.xAxis); circles = qGeometry(rim, GeometryType.CIRCLE)
one opChamfer EQUAL_OFFSETS width 1 on qUnion([lines, circles]): the two long top edges (along local x) and the bore's top rim (a 1 mm countersink)
construction.notes: Plain Boolean on purpose (no coplanar merge), so the zone does not inherit AC11's merge contract; its verdict is routed through the query results. The countersink (radius 3 at the top) stays 2 mm clear of both chamfers.

outcomes.note: plate with a countersunk through-bore and two chamfered long top edges

silentWrong: plane test ignores the plane offset (bottom face selected too): the long bottom edges and the bottom bore rim are chamfered as well
direction filter against a world axis: under V2 the short top edges (local y) are chamfered instead of the long ones
empty query under V1/V3 treated as success with nothing chamfered (V = 1536 - 32*pi)
bore rim missed by qGeometry(CIRCLE), or both bore rims chamfered

zones.title: Round bar with a through-bore and a hex pocket, one cut
zones.intent: A bar (cylinder r 10, h 12) loses a coaxial through-bore r 2 and a hexagonal pocket (across flats 10, irrational corners from h = 5/sqrt(3)) 4 deep from the top face, both tools in one subtraction. Tests a mixed cylinder/prism tool arrangement in one Boolean where the tools overlap (the bore runs through the pocket floor), genus 1.

steps: fCylinder bottomCenter (0,0,0) topCenter (0,0,12) radius 10 (the bar)
fCylinder bottomCenter (0,0,-1) topCenter (0,0,13) radius 2 (the through-bore tool, overhangs both faces by 1)

h = 5/sqrt(3) (FS: const h = 5 / sqrt(3)); sketch on the local plane z = 8: closed skPolyline (2h,0),(h,5),(-h,5),(-2h,0),(-h,-5),(h,-5),(2h,0); opExtrude 5 along local +z (the pocket tool, z 8..13, overhangs the top by 1)
one opTransform(toWorld(cs)) on the bar and both tools
one opBoolean SUBTRACTION target bar, tools bore and pocket prism (both tools in one cut; they overlap in z 8..12)
V4: bar radius 10.025, bore radius 2.025; the hexagon is unchanged
V5: the bore tool as skCircle centre (0,0) r 2 on the local plane z = -1 extruded 14 along local +z instead of fCylinder; the same pocket tool, opTransform and single cut
construction.notes: Walls: bore to the hexagon flats 3 mm, hexagon corners (circumradius 10/sqrt(3) = 5.77) to the bar wall 4.23 mm, pocket floor 8 mm above the bottom. The hexagon corners are irrational; the payload corners (binary64) differ from the nominal ones by about 1e-15 mm and the closed form is the nominal hexagon (closed-forms.py also integrates the payload corners).

b3dFeatures: BuildSketch + Polyline + make_face (hexagon corners from the apothem and math.sqrt)

outcomes.note: bar with a through-bore and a hexagonal pocket, genus 1

silentWrong: pocket floor at the wrong depth or the pocket not open at the top
bore missing below the pocket floor or blind
hexagon rotated, scaled or replaced by a circle

zones.title: Pattern copies as drilling tools
zones.intent: A 32x24x8 box; a seed cylinder r 2 at (8,12) through it; opPattern copies the seed by transform(vector) 8 and 16 mm along local x; the seed and both copies are subtracted in one Boolean. Tests pattern instances used as Boolean tools, genus 3.

steps: fCuboid corner1 (0,0,0) corner2 (32,24,8)
fCylinder bottomCenter (8,12,-1) topCenter (8,12,9) radius 2 (the seed tool, overhangs both faces by 1)
opPattern of the seed body with transforms [transform(vector(8,0,0) mm), transform(vector(16,0,0) mm)] and instanceNames ["1","2"] (local coordinates)
one opTransform(toWorld(cs)) on the box, the seed and both copies
one opBoolean SUBTRACTION target box, tools seed and copies
V4: seed radius 2.025
V5: the seed as skCircle centre (8,12) r 2 on the local plane z = -1 extruded 10 along local +z instead of fCylinder; the same opPattern, opTransform and single cut
construction.notes: Bore to bore 4 mm, bores to the walls 6 mm (x) and 10 mm (y). The copies are pattern instances, never separate fCylinder calls.

b3dFeatures: seed copies moved by Location (the pattern transforms)

outcomes.note: box with three through-bores in a row, genus 3

silentWrong: only the seed subtracts (copies ignored or left as extra bodies)
copies along another axis or at the wrong spacing
a copy doubled onto the seed

zones.title: Cut into a concave extrusion profile
zones.intent: An L-shaped profile (0,0),(24,0),(24,6),(6,6),(6,20),(0,20) extruded 6 loses a 2x2 square cutter [2,4]x[8,10] through its upright leg in one subtraction (V5: the L as a chain of skLineSegment). Tests a Boolean cut whose target faces (the L caps) are non-convex: the notch stays open, genus 1.

steps: sketch on the local plane z = 0 (plane(vector(0,0,0) mm, vector(0,0,1), vector(1,0,0))): closed skPolyline (0,0),(24,0),(24,6),(6,6),(6,20),(0,20),(0,0); opExtrude 6 along local +z, entities qSketchRegion(sketchId, false) (the L prism)
fCuboid corner1 (2,8,-1) corner2 (4,10,7) (the square cutter, overhangs both caps by 1)
one opTransform(toWorld(cs)) on the L prism and the cutter
opBoolean SUBTRACTION target L prism, tool cutter
V5: the L outline as six skLineSegment calls chained end to start ((0,0)->(24,0)->(24,6)->(6,6)->(6,20)->(0,20)->(0,0)) instead of one skPolyline; the same extrusion, cutter, opTransform and cut
construction.notes: Cutter to the upright's faces x = 0 and x = 6 2 mm, to the notch level y = 6 2 mm, to the upright's end y = 20 10 mm. The target caps are non-convex (the L); the cutter lies in the upright, not at the notch.

zones.title: Moved body stays editable
zones.intent: A 24x16x8 block built at the local origin is moved by opTransform with transform(vector(40,8,0)), then a through-bore r 2 at (52,16), the moved block's centre, is subtracted (V5: the same move written toWorld(coordSystem(...))). Tests that a body moved with transform(vector) stays a valid Boolean target at its new place; genus 1.

opTransform of the block with transform(vector(40,8,0) mm) (local coordinates, like AC71's pattern transforms): the block now spans [40,64]x[8,24]x[0,8]

zones.title: PH-cubic arch prism (explicit skBezier)
zones.intent: An arch bounded by one cubic skBezier with the control points (0,0), (8,6), (18,6), (26,0) and the chord (26,0)-(0,0), extruded 4 (V5: the same curve written as its exact degree-4 elevation). The cubic has a Pythagorean hodograph, |C'(t)| = 6(2t^2 - 2t + 5), so its arc length, unit normals and every closed form are rational. Tests a spline profile edge (control points, not interpolated points), its extrusion surface and exact spline measures.

steps: sketch on plane(cs): skBezier with points (0,0), (8,6), (18,6), (26,0) (control points, degree 3) and skLineSegment (26,0)->(0,0), the chord closing the arch
opExtrude qSketchRegion(sketchId, false) 4 along cs.zAxis
V5: the same sketch with skBezier points (0,0), (6,4.5), (13,6), (20,4.5), (26,0): the exact degree-4 elevation of the V0 cubic (Q_i = (i/4) P_(i-1) + (1 - i/4) P_i), the same curve
construction.notes: Every control point is an integer or a dyadic mm value; the kernel receives them as binary64 metres (E9), about 1e-16 relative from the decimal closed form, far inside the exact band. The arch is a graph over x (x'(t) = 12(2 + t - t^2) > 0 on [0,1]) and meets the chord only at its ends (y = 18t(1 - t)); its curvature radius is at least 81/4 = 20.25 (at the apex).

Bezier from the five degree-4 control points (V5)

zones.title: Spur gear with hub and bore, one sketch (skBezier flanks)
zones.intent: A 16-tooth spur gear (module 1.5, pressure angle 20 deg, addendum 1 module, dedendum 1.25 modules, tooth 0 centred on +x) whose outline is one sketch: per tooth two cubic skBezier flanks (the Hermite cubic of the involute from the base circle to the tip circle, handles 1/16 and 5/8 of the chord along the end tangents), a three-point tip arc, two radial lines from the root circle up to the base circle and a three-point root arc. Extruded 6, a hub r 6 from z 6 to 12 united, a bore r 2.5 subtracted through gear and hub (V5: fCylinder hub and a bore tool with 1 mm overshoot). Every control is computed in FeatureScript with cos/sin/tan/atan/sqrt: binary64 payloads. Tests spline flanks meeting tangent radial lines, 96 curves and lines in one loop, and a spline prism stacked with round operands. Distilled from first principles; no CADBench part is copied.

steps: FeatureScript payload, in this order (all lengths mm): rp = m*z/2, rb = rp*cos(alpha) with alpha = 20*degree, ra = rp + m, rf = rp - 1.25*m, psib = PI/(2*z) + tan(alpha) - alpha/radian, ta = sqrt(ra*ra/(rb*rb) - 1), psia = psib - (ta - atan(ta)/radian), pitch = 2*PI/z; tooth k: th = k*pitch

per tooth k and side s (+1 upper, -1 lower): a0 = th + s*psib, a3 = th + s*psia, a1 = a0 - s*ta; base point B = rb*(cos a0, sin a0), root foot F = rf*(cos a0, sin a0), tip point T = ra*(cos a3, sin a3), chord c = sqrt((T - B).(T - B)); flank skBezier points B, B + 0.0625*c*(cos a0, sin a0), T - 0.625*c*(cos a1, sin a1), T

one sketch on the local plane z = 0 (plane(vector(0,0,0), vector(0,0,1), vector(1,0,0))): per tooth skLineSegment F_lower -> B_lower, the lower skBezier, skArc start T_lower mid ra*(cos th, sin th) end T_upper, the upper skBezier, skLineSegment B_upper -> F_upper, skArc start F_upper mid rf*(cos(th + pitch/2), sin(th + pitch/2)) end F_lower of tooth k + 1 (shared points are the same computed values); opExtrude qSketchRegion(sketchId, false) 6 along local +z

hub: skCircle centre (0,0) r 6 on the local plane z = 6, opExtrude 6 along local +z; bore tool: skCircle centre (0,0) r 2.5 on the local plane z = 0, opExtrude 12 (flush with the gear bottom and the hub top)
one opTransform(toWorld(cs)) on gear, hub and bore tool; opBoolean UNION of gear and hub; opBoolean SUBTRACTION of the bore tool
V4: hub radius 6.025, bore radius 2.525 (the gear outline stays)
V5: hub fCylinder (0,0,6)-(0,0,12) r 6 and bore fCylinder (0,0,-1)-(0,0,13) r 2.5 (1 mm overshoot through both faces) instead of the sketch circles; the same gear sketch, opTransform and Booleans
construction.notes: Nominal data: rb = 11.2763114494, rf = 10.125 < rb (radial lines of 1.15131 mm), ra = 13.5, psib = 0.1130791543, psia = 0.03698338037 rad; flank chord 2.4136828 mm, length 2.444242261 mm, deviation from the involute at most 0.00387 mm; cap area 438.008481544518 mm^2 vs the true involute gear 437.84609806942 mm^2 (relative 0.000371, inside the 1e-3 sanity bound). At the base circle the flank's tangent is radial: the flank and its radial line meet G1 up to the payload rounding (about 1e-16 rad) and stay two edges and two faces. The hub (r 6) lies inside the root circle (10.125); the bore tool is flush with the gear bottom and the hub top (E4 contact at equal levels in the construction frame). The levels are E9-exact: the hub top is its sketch plane plus its extrusion, fl(0.006) + fl(0.006) = 2 fl(0.006) = fl(0.012) m, the bore top exactly; a 5 mm hub would not be (fl(0.006) + fl(0.005) exceeds fl(0.011) by 8.7e-19 m, a membrane over the bore for an exact kernel).

b3dFeatures: Bezier from the contract poles (FS payload replicated in binary64) + Line + ThreePointArc + make_face

volume.derivation: gear prism 6*A (A = 438.00848154451809598) plus the hub above it pi*6^2*6 minus the bore through gear and hub pi*(5/2)^2*12. cap area A: tooth k of z = 16 centred at 2 pi k/z; base radius rb = rp cos(alpha), tip ra, root rf; flank half-angles psib (base) and psia (tip) from the involute function; the upper flank of tooth 0 is the cubic Bezier B = (x0,y0) -> T = (x3,y3) with handles c/16 (radial) and 5c/8 (involute tangent at the tip, direction psib - ta); S = 1/2 int (x dy - y dx) over it (the Bernstein bilinear form, /20). Sector form of Green's theorem about the gear centre: radial lines add 0, the tip arc ra^2 psia, the two root half arcs rf^2 (pi/z - psib), the two flanks -2S. The FeatureScript builds binary64 payload controls (cos, sin, tan, atan, sqrt, then * millimeter); their exact Green area (Fractions, three-point arcs through the payload points) differs from this nominal value by about 1e-15 relative

area.derivation: two caps 2A (the bottom cap loses the bore disc, the gear top the hub footprint), the gear side 6*P, the hub wall 2*pi*6*6, the hub top pi*(6^2 - (5/2)^2), the bore wall 2*pi*(5/2)*12; P = z(2L + 2(rb - rf) + 2 ra psia + rf(2 pi/z - 2 psib)) with the flank arc length L by quadrature (50 digits)

topology.derivation: per tooth 6 side faces (2 flank extrusions, 2 radial planes, the tip and the root cylinder) = 96, plus the bottom cap (outer outline, bore circle), the gear top (outline, hub circle), the hub wall, the hub top (rim, bore circle) and the bore wall = 101 faces (Plane 35, Cylinder 34, SurfaceOfExtrusion 32); 96 outline vertices per cap = 192; 96 edges per cap + 96 vertical + 4 ring edges (bore at z 0 and 12, hub at z 6 and 12) = 292; loops 96 + 2*5 = 106; genus 1 (the bore). The flank meets its radial line tangentially (G1 at the base circle up to rounding) but they are distinct faces and never merged

bbox.derivation: tooth k is centred at 2 pi k/z; teeth 0, 4, 8 and 12 put their tip arcs (ra = 27/2) across the +x, +y, -x and -y axes; the hub top is at z 12. Every flank point lies inside the convex hull of the tip arcs, so V3 is the tight AABB of the rotated tip arcs (z 0 and 6) and hub rim (z 12)
